properties.title: AI-Augmented Adaptive Digital Twin Modeling for Brain Tumor Evolution Prediction and Treatment Scheduling

properties.name: Adaptive RD–residual brain-tumor twin with scenario MPC
properties.membership: Core hybrid learned temporal simulator and decision-coupled synthetic controller
properties.architecture: Interpretable cellularity field plus chemo/RT exposure states evolve by reaction–diffusion;3D U-Net residual correction trained offline, updated from observed synthetic transitions with3-step rollout loss; random-shooting robust MPC ranks120 schedules over10 modeldays and executes first action.

properties.design: 387 patient-imaging-initialized synthetic120step trajectories;80/10/10 patient split,38 test trajectories. Reference simulator differs by spatial proliferation; no observed longitudinal clinical outcome target.

assertions.rationale: Explicit120 model-integration-day grid and121stored states define native synthetic time.
Clinical masks/continuous maps aligned/resampled to128cubed using distinct interpolation.
Patient-level split separates anatomy/init; development action histories generated separately from heldout scheduling runs.
3D U-Net encodes cellularity plus constant chemo/RT action maps.
Weighted voxel residual-target loss trains predicted next state.
Cellularity and decaying chemo/RT exposure states carried across transitions.
Recent patient-specific synthetic observations update residual-network weights while RD fixed.
Treatment exposure states retain previous therapy and current cellularity carries history.
Explicit decaying exposure states persist prior treatment effects.
Cellularity field, compartment exposures, burden, diffusion/growth parameters have explicit physiological meanings.
Chemo and RT actions separately condition RD and learned residual.
Chemo0–25integer actionunits and RT2Gy computational actions defined.
Eligibility every7steps fromstep1; onceonlyRT and120step course explicit.
Mutually exclusive none/chemo/RT and retained decaying exposures define joint-update semantics.
Dose/timing/modality and toxicity constraints restrict candidates.
RD plus exposure updates advance cellularity one modelday.
Learned residual correction operationally augments mechanistic transition.
Fixed RD backbone plus learned/adapted U-Net discrepancy is explicit coupling.
Reactiondiffusion and treatment exposure kinetics constrain transition; brain mask/clipping constrain output.
Adaptation unrolls3steps, scores only observed offsets.
Hybrid correction emits next3D cellularity field.
Cellularity maps integrate to tumor burden and toxicity state supplies constraint readout.
Full120step rollout consumes prior generated cellularity, separately from reference-conditioned pairs.
120steps at1model-integrationday, MPC10steps.
Adapted twin forward simulates120candidate schedules.
Terminal-burden objective is explicit outside forward dynamics; discussion notes cumulative-burden tradeoff.
Worst-case rank under two bounded state perturbations changes selected schedule.
120random-shooting candidates sampled under specified dose/timing/toxicity bounds; no globaloptimum claimed.
Toxicity-violating chemo replaced by no treatment; applies computational candidate screen only.
Explicit bounded two-scenario uncertainty set around current state, without probability or calibration claims.
Action-conditioned one-step and closedloop schedule evaluations reported.
Heldout reference-conditioned one-step evaluated separately.
Recursive MSE/Dice/burden tracked to120steps.
Operational MPC schedules tested using reference simulator.
First action executed in simulator, new observation updates residual before replanning.
Actions advance reference simulator to supply next observation; in-silico closedloop only.
Fixed and MPC schedules compared from same heldout initialization under shared reference dynamics.
Heldout successor prediction errors measured. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Free-running120step error and adaptation results reported. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

Alternative schedules replayed under matched simulator initializations. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

Terminal/cumulativeburden, dose andtoxicity compare controller andfixedschedule. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

Observation-schedule sensitivity test dense vs sparse is reported with configuration confounding. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Schedules replay through distinct referenceproliferation dynamics, but no broader adversarial/exploitation stress protocol or supporttest.
criteria_met: Different simulator replay of optimized plans

assertions.rationale: New observations update residualparameters before replanning; direct posterior current-state measurement correction not specified.
Patient-specific observation updates residual network, not a separate measured-state filtering distribution.
No new participants; public deidentified UPENN imaging and synthetic longitudinal data scope explicitly declared.

evidence_fragments.content:
Experiments were conducted using synthetic longitudinal tumor trajectories initialized from
patient-specific clinical imaging. Anatomical brain masks, tissue maps, ADC images, and tumor
regions were derived from the publicly available UPENN-GBM cohort [4]. Because frequently sam-
pled longitudinal imaging under controlled treatment conditions is rarely available at cohort scale,
clinical imaging was used to define patient-specific anatomy and tumor initialization, while subse-
quent tumor evolution was generated computationally. Throughout this section and the Results,
“reference” denotes a simulator-generated tumor trajectory.
For each patient, the initial tumor state was constructed using the formulation in Section 3.1. In
the present implementation,ADCref was estimated as the 99th percentile of valid ADC values within
the tumor region, with the brain mask used as a fallback when the tumor region was too small. All
patient-specific fields were aligned to a common voxel space and resampled to a128×128×128
computational grid. Discrete masks were resampled using nearest-neighbor interpolation, whereas
continuous imaging-derived quantities were resampled using trilinear interpolation.
Each patient-specific initial tumor state was propagated for 120 simulation steps, producing 120
one-step transitions and 121 stored states, including the initial state at step 0. Under the present
parameterization, one simulation step corresponds to one model-integration day. The term “simu-
lation step” is used throughout the experimental analysis to distinguish this numerical resolution
from the frequency of clinically available observations. A total of 387 patient-informed synthetic
trajectories were generated. The data were partitioned at the patient level into training, validation,
and testing cohorts using an 80%/10%/10% split. Patient-level separation ensured that anatomy
and tumor initialization from a given patient appeared in only one partition.
Each trajectory contained both tumor states and the treatment actions applied during trajectory
generation. Treatment histories used for residual-model development were generated in separate
controller runs and were not derived from the held-out treatment-scheduling experiments. The
resulting transitions had the form(Nj, aj, Nj+1), wherea j denotes the treatment action applied at
simulation stepj. The detailed action space and feasibility constraints used to generate treatment-
conditioned trajectories are described in Section 4.5. The principal dataset and prediction settings
are summarized in Table 1.

evidence_fragments.content:
The residual correction model was implemented as a 3D U-Net based on established volumetric
U-Net architectures [45–47]. The network received three input channels: the current tumor state,
a chemotherapy-action map, and a radiotherapy-action map. The two treatment-action maps were
spatially constant over the computational domain and encoded the applied actionaj. Chemotherapy
and radiotherapy values were normalized by their respective maximum values in the training set
before being expanded into spatially constant maps. The network produced a voxel-wise residual
field with the same spatial dimensions as the tumor state.
The encoder used feature widths of 24, 48, and 96, followed by a 192-channel bottleneck. The
decoder used trilinear upsampling and skip connections. Residual convolutional blocks used instance
normalization and LeakyReLU activation. A dropout rate of 0.1 was applied at the bottleneck, and
the network output was multiplied by a learnable residual scale initialized to 0.1. Offline residual
learning used the weighted objective defined in Section 3.1. The residual-weighting parameters were
set toα= 10andτ res = 10 −4. Training used32×32×323D patches sampled from treatment-
conditioned trajectories. The model was optimized using AdamW for 200 epochs with a batch size
of 12, learning rate10−4, and weight decay10−5. The gradient norm was clipped at 1.0.

The median
final tumor burden was 4,610 [2,696, 5,599] under the fixed schedule and 3,601 [2,085, 4,368] under
adapted MPC. Across paired patients, the median relative reduction in final tumor burden was
22.4%. The two strategies used similar total chemotherapy exposure (136 versus 134 action units at
the cohort median)and identical radiotherapyexposure(2 Gy atthe cohortmedian). MPC operated
closer to the prescribed chemotherapy-toxicity limit. Median maximum toxicity increased from 3.65
under the fixed schedule to 4.98 under MPC, while remaining below the threshold of 5.0, and no
toxicity violations were observed. In contrast to final burden, median cumulative tumor burden was
higher under MPC: 859,409 [518,067, 1,036,383] compared with 677,145 [412,212, 816,161] under
the fixed schedule.
The paired comparison in Fig. 12 shows the same tradeoff at the patient level. MPC reduces
final tumor burden for most patients but increases cumulative burden for most patients. This
behavior is consistent with the controller objective, which prioritizes worst-case terminal tumor
burden over the finite planning horizon rather than cumulative burden over the complete trajec-
tory. Thus, the scheduling experiment demonstrates that the adapted DT can be incorporated into
constrained receding-horizon treatment planning, while also showing that the resulting treatment
behavior depends strongly on the chosen optimization objective.

Validation used patient-informed synthetic trajectories rather than observed longitudinal out-

and treatment response. The model omits treatment resistance and imaging uncertainty, while

legacy_cells.C: Liu, Wenxi, Trimboli, Michael, Li, Xianqi
legacy_cells.S: Can an adaptive tumor-state model forecast brain-tumor evolution under chemotherapy and radiotherapy and use the forecasts to select constrained treatment schedules?
legacy_cells.V: Compare chemotherapy/radiotherapy schedules to minimize worst-case terminal tumor burden subject to timing, dose, toxicity, and bounded-state-perturbation constraints; evaluated computationally.
legacy_cells.AI: 3D anatomical brain masks; tissue maps; apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) images; tumor segmentations/states; chemotherapy and radiotherapy action maps; simulator-generated longitudinal tumor trajectories
legacy_cells.AQ: Temporal resampling/observation-clock preservation was not assessed; the paper separately tested observations every seven simulation steps.
legacy_cells.AT: Residual-network parameters are updated using a masked rollout loss on newly available tumor-state observations; the reaction–diffusion backbone remains fixed.
legacy_cells.AZ: Explicit normalized cellularity-like tumor field N(x,t) in 3D; total tumor burden is derived by summing the field over voxels.
legacy_cells.BD: Mutually exclusive none/chemotherapy/radiotherapy; chemotherapy sampled as integer action units 0–25; radiotherapy is a 2-Gy action, at most once; treatment eligible every seven simulation steps.
legacy_cells.BF: One modality per decision step; treatment eligible every seven simulation steps; chemotherapy action units 0–25; radiotherapy at most once at 2 Gy; chemotherapy violating toxicity limit is replaced by no treatment; toxicity limit 5.
legacy_cells.BL: One model-integration day per simulation step; trajectory length 120 simulation steps.
legacy_cells.BN: Tissue-dependent reaction–diffusion with logistic proliferation, anatomical brain-domain masking/clipping, and explicit decaying chemotherapy/radiotherapy exposure states.
legacy_cells.BS: Next-step and recursively forecast 3D tumor cellularity-state voxel field; derived tumor burden; treatment schedules from MPC.
legacy_cells.BU: MPC minimizes worst-case terminal tumor burden over the planning horizon; chemotherapy toxicity is constrained to toxmax = 5.
legacy_cells.BV: Weighted voxel-wise residual-correction loss for offline one-step learning; masked reconstruction loss over an H=3 rollout for patient-specific adaptation.
legacy_cells.CD: 120 simulation steps for forecasting rollout; MPC planning horizon 10 simulation steps.
legacy_cells.CK: Select the sampled schedule minimizing worst-case terminal tumor burden across two bounded state-perturbation scenarios; enforce treatment timing/dose and chemotherapy toxicity constraints (toxmax = 5).
legacy_cells.DN: University of Pennsylvania Glioblastoma (UPENN-GBM) cohort; patient-informed synthetic longitudinal tumor trajectories
legacy_cells.DQ: 387 patient-informed synthetic trajectories; 38 held-out test patients reported for recursive forecasting and treatment-scheduling results.
legacy_cells.DX: Held-out reference-conditioned one-step prediction, dense sampling: masked voxel-wise MSE 2.26×10⁻³ (RD) vs 3.54×10⁻⁴ (hybrid); Dice 0.641 vs 0.920; PSNR 29.85 vs 36.99 dB; burden error 12,765 vs 2,458 mm³. Sparse hybrid MSE 4.05×10⁻⁴; Dice 0.868; PSNR 35.51 dB; burden error 4,846 mm³.
legacy_cells.EA: Treatment schedules were checked against modality/timing/dose and toxicity constraints; both strategies had zero toxicity-violation steps, and MPC maximum toxicity remained below the stated 5.0 limit.
legacy_cells.EB: In simulator-replay comparisons across 38 held-out patients, online-adapted MPC had a 22.4% median paired reduction in final tumor burden versus the fixed schedule, but higher median cumulative burden (859,409 vs 677,145).
legacy_cells.EC: Simulator-replay decision outcome: median paired final tumor burden decreased 22.4% under online-adapted MPC versus the fixed schedule; cumulative burden increased.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with RD baseline and offline hybrid RD–residual model: dense reference-conditioned MSE 2.26×10⁻³, 3.54×10⁻⁴; Dice 0.641, 0.920. In recursive forecasting, online adaptation improved versus offline hybrid on reported cohort medians (MSE 1.64×10⁻³ to 8.87×10⁻⁴; Dice 0.743 to 0.814).
legacy_cells.EL: Offline hybrid recursive rollout worsened MSE versus RD (1.64×10⁻³ vs 1.57×10⁻³); under sparse observations adaptation worsened MSE (2.66×10⁻³ vs 2.31×10⁻³) and burden error (1.24×10⁴ vs 1.11×10⁴ mm³). A patient example showed large transient late-rollout MSE increases.
legacy_cells.EM: Computational action constraints include mutual exclusion of treatment modalities, dose/timing limits, chemotherapy toxicity threshold toxmax = 5, and replacing a chemotherapy action that violates toxicity with no treatment.
legacy_cells.EO: The imaging cohort is described as publicly available and de-identified; no new human or animal participants were enrolled.
legacy_cells.FL: Imaging-derived anatomy, tissue maps, ADC and tumor initialization define a 3D voxel tumor state; a mechanistic reaction–diffusion transition is corrected by a 3D U-Net residual network, updated from observations, and coupled to random-shooting scenario MPC for constrained chemotherapy/radiotherapy scheduling.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors introduce a hybrid reaction–diffusion/residual tumor model, update the residual during recursive forecasting from patient-specific observations, and couple the adapted model to scenario-based MPC for treatment-scheduling evaluation.
legacy_cells.FN: In synthetic validation, dense one-step hybrid prediction reduced MSE by 84.3% versus RD and increased Dice by 43.5%; adaptation reduced recursive MSE by 45.9% versus offline hybrid; MPC yielded 22.4% median paired reduction in final tumor burden versus fixed schedule.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors state that validation used patient-informed synthetic rather than observed longitudinal outcomes; treatment resistance and imaging uncertainty are omitted; chemo/radiotherapy/toxicity dynamics are simplified; sparse-observation adaptation remains limited; MPC uncertainty covers bounded tumor-state perturbations, not model parameters, treatment response, or future observations.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors propose validation in longitudinal animal tumor models with repeated imaging, controlled treatment delivery, biological response, and terminal histopathology, followed by clinical studies using real longitudinal imaging and delivered-treatment records.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify sparse, irregular, treatment-confounded clinical follow-up as limiting identification of patient-specific tumor dynamics and evaluation of alternative treatment trajectories; controlled patient-informed synthetic settings are used for systematic evaluation.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to patient-informed synthetic trajectories and a controlled simulator, not clinical longitudinal outcomes or patient benefit. Action-conditioned simulations and schedule comparisons do not establish identified causal treatment effects in patients; sparse-observation results degraded density/burden metrics, and the objective traded higher cumulative burden for lower terminal burden.
